# Energy Research Warehouse (ERW): briefing for AI assistants

The Energy Research Warehouse (ERW) is the live, citable record of the US
energy system: prices, flows, projects, deals and policy across power, natural
gas, oil, nuclear, renewables, storage and transmission, with the global prices
and events that move US markets included. AI's demand for power is the sharpest
current lens on that system, not its boundary. US first, world later. Every
source is reshaped into one of three standard table shapes, and every row
traces to the report it came from. (Elsewhere "ERW" can mean enhanced rock
weathering. Not here.)

Modeled on the IRW's llms.txt (itemresponsewarehouse.org). Owner documents if
this file and they disagree: docs/datastandard.md (format), docs/coverage.md
and warehouse/metadata/coverage.csv (what exists, generated daily), the latest
archive/sessions/SESSION_*_REPORT.md (what changed). Table names, spans and row counts move
daily: check `erw.coverage()` (or the list_tables tool) before answering from
memory or from this file.


## 1. Three shapes

**series**: one row per observation, key (entity, variable, ts_utc).
  entity    `namespace:id`: `ercot:HB_NORTH`, `eia930:CISO`, `eia:henry_hub`,
            `eia:WCESTUS1`, `fred:DCOILWTICO`, `pjm:RTO`
  variable  what was measured: `spp_dam`, `lmp_rtm_15m_mean`, `demand_mw`,
            `net_generation_solar_mw`, `spot_price`, `stocks`, `peak_iqr`
  ts_utc    START of the interval, UTC. Daily and longer series (P1D, P1W, P1M,
            P1Y) put the date the source reports at 00:00Z: a date, not an instant
  value     float, in `unit`; unit, freq (PT15M, PT1H, P1D, P1W, P1M, P3M, P1Y),
            geo (ISO 3166-2), market, node, source, source_url, retrieved_at, vintage
**entities**: one row per physical or corporate thing, key entity_id.
  entity_id, entity_type, name, geo, lat, lon, capacity_mw, status,
  status_date, operator, source, source_url, retrieved_at, vintage, then the
  source's own columns (EIA-860M: state, county, balancing_authority,
  technology, technology_group, energy_source, nameplate_mw, net_summer_mw, ...;
  queues: queue_id, poi, zone, fuel_technology, iso_status, queue_date, ...)
**events**: one row per story, deal or filing, key event_id.
  event_id, event_date (a date, or a UTC time), event_type, parties, entity_ids,
  mw, price, currency, status, source, source_url, then the table's own columns.

Every CSV starts with `#` provenance lines (source report, URL, retrieval
time, run log, series names, notes, license). `erw.fetch` parses them into
`df.attrs["erw"]`. Reading a CSV without the package: skip those lines by
count; never `pandas.read_csv(comment="#")`, which cuts every URL with a `#`.


## 2. The table families

**Partition columns** (session 29, docs/datastandard.md decision 28): a table
  that holds several ISOs, BAs or years says which in a column, never in its
  name. Filter on it: `market` (ercot_dam, caiso_rtm, ...; the trader view:
  ercot, caiso, ...), `ba` (EIA-930: ciso, erco, ...), `year` (the ERCOT
  history). Old names such as ercot_dam_hub_prices or eia930_ciso_demand are
  gone from the catalogue; the map is warehouse/metadata/table_migrations.csv.
**ISO power prices, live windows** (series, USD/MWh), rolling about 30 days,
day-ahead tables running into tomorrow:
  iso_dam_hub_prices and iso_rtm_hub_prices: CAISO, ERCOT, MISO and SPP hubs,
    one market per ISO (market = ercot_dam, caiso_rtm, miso_dam, spp_dam, ...):
    ERCOT (spp_dam PT1H, spp_rtm PT15M): 6 hubs HB_BUSAVG, HB_HOUSTON,
      HB_HUBAVG, HB_NORTH, HB_SOUTH, HB_WEST
    CAISO (lmp_dam, lmp_rtm_15m_mean): TH_NP15_GEN-APND, TH_SP15_GEN-APND,
      TH_ZP26_GEN-APND
    MISO (lmp_dam, hourly lmp_rtm): 8 hubs
    SPP (lmp_dam; lmp_rtm_15m_mean, a short window): SPPNORTH_HUB, SPPSOUTH_HUB
  nyiso_dam_zone_prices, nyiso_rtm_zone_prices (lmp_rtm_15m_mean): 11 zones
  isone_dam_zone_prices, isone_rtm_zone_prices (lmp_rtm_15m_mean),
    isone_rtm_zone_prices_hourly (lmp_rtm): .H.INTERNAL_HUB and 8 zones
**ERCOT history, 2015 to today, one table**: ercot_all_hub_prices_history,
  day-ahead and real-time (market = ercot_dam or ercot_rtm), same 6 hubs,
  `year` = the ERCOT operating year (Central time, so 1 January's first UTC
  hours belong to the year before). Complete from 2015-01-01; about three
  million rows, so always filter (market, year, node, start, end). The current
  year stops where the live window starts; the two never overlap. A question
  about ERCOT before the live window (last year, 2021, "since 2015") goes here.
**Derived: ERCOT peak premium** (method docs/methods/ercot_peak_premium.md):
  ercot_peak_premium_annual (P1Y) and ercot_peak_premium_monthly (P1M), per
  hub, from every 15-minute real-time interval since 2015. Variables:
  {overnight,midday,peak,all}_{min,q1,median,q3,max}, all_p999, peak_iqr,
  all_iqr, worst_interval_multiple (P99.9 / median), peak_minus_midday_median,
  n_scarcity (intervals >= 1,000 USD/MWh), n_negative (<= 0), n_intervals.
  Blocks by local (America/Chicago) hour of interval start: overnight 21 to
  12, midday 12 to 16, peak 16 to 21. ts_utc labels the local year or month.
  The current year and month are partial (n_intervals says how much).
**Derived: trader view** (session 19, method docs/methods/trader_view.md):
  iso_trader_daily for ercot, caiso, nyiso, miso, spp, isone (market = the
  iso, node = the hub or zone, ts_utc = the local operating day): da_mean_usd,
  da_onpeak_mean_usd (5x16: hours starting 06:00 to 21:00 local, weekdays not
  NERC holidays), da_offpeak_mean_usd, rt_mean_usd, da_rt_spread_mean_usd and
  da_rt_spread_max_usd (real-time minus day-ahead, hourly), hours_rt_over_da_50
  (count), implied_heat_rate (MMBtu/MWh: da_mean_usd over Henry Hub spot),
  da_volatility_30d_usd (standard deviation of 30 day-over-day changes in
  da_mean_usd; USD/MWh, not annualized). SPP has day-ahead metrics only (no SPP
  real-time table); PJM is absent (no licensed PJM data).
  iso_rt_top_intervals: a snapshot of each ISO's 10 highest real-time
  intervals of its latest 7 complete local days.
**Derived: price board v2** (session 30, method docs/methods/price_board.md; the
  site's /board). Means of complete local operating days only; variables carry
  the market, da_ or rt_. price_board_latest: every hub and zone of the six
  ISOs: {da,rt}_daily_mean (last 30 days), _latest_day_mean,
  _previous_day_mean, _day_change (USD/MWh), _day_change_pct, _avg_7d,
  _avg_30d, _min_30d, _max_30d (of the daily means), _days_7d, _days_30d,
  _latest_interval, _intervals_30d, and da_minus_rt. price_board_peak_offpeak:
  each ISO's main hub, {da,rt}_{peak,offpeak,all}_mean and _peak_minus_offpeak
  per day (P1D, last 90 days the tables reach; peak = hours ending 7 to 22,
  Mon to Fri, CAISO Mon to Sat, NERC holidays off-peak), and ERCOT HB_HUBAVG
  per operating year since 2015 ({da,rt}_year_{all_mean,peak_mean,
  offpeak_mean,peak_minus_offpeak,days}, P1Y, means; ercot_peak_premium_annual has
  the medians). price_board_spreads: henry_hub, per main hub spark_spread_7
  (day-ahead daily mean minus an ASSUMED 7.0 MMBtu/MWh times Henry Hub; say
  it is an assumption), implied_heat_rate, da_daily_mean, and
  brent_minus_wti; x_gas_date is the Henry Hub date used. price_board_carbon
  is internal (CARB and RGGI).
**EIA-930 hourly grid data** (series, MW): eia930_all_demand (demand_mw,
  demand_forecast_mw) and eia930_all_generation (net_generation_mw and
  net_generation_<fuel>_mw: coal, natural_gas, nuclear, solar, wind, hydro,
  battery, oil, other, ...), column `ba` = ciso, erco, isne, miso, nyis, pjm,
  swpp, us48 (entity eia930:CISO, ...). About 30 days.
**Interchange and the grid network** (session 49, method docs/methods/grid_network.md):
  eia930_all_interchange: EIA-930 hourly interchange between balancing
  authorities, every pair EIA reports, interchange_mw, MW (EIA's MWh per hour),
  positive when the reporting BA (column ba, lowercase; entity eia930:<FROM>-<TO>)
  exports to its neighbor (x_to_ba). Both BAs of a pair report it. From
  2026-09-13, grown daily; not in the live set (hourly history).
  grid_network_nodes (derived): one entity per BA, demand_mw and
  intensity_generation (the latest hour, the seven ISO BAs) and
  interchange_volume_mwh over the latest 168 hours; x_name is EIA's name.
  grid_network_links (derived): each BA pair once per hour, the last 168 hours,
  flow_mw positive when the code that sorts first exports to the other.
  eia930_daily_total_interchange (session 68): EIA's own daily total
  interchange of every BA (type TI), total_interchange_mwh, positive when the BA
  exports, EIA's Eastern day, from 2019; history, not in the live set.
  eia930_event_hourly_interchange (session 68): hourly interchange_mw of every
  pair and demand_mw of every BA for two windows only, column event = uri_2021
  (2021-02-07 to 02-24) or east_heat_2025 (2025-06-20 to 06-28); history.
  ba_supply_monthly (derived, session 68): who supplies a grid. Positive means
  the NEIGHBOUR SUPPLIED the BA (the opposite of EIA's sign). Pair entity
  eia930:<BA>-<NEIGHBOUR>: net_import_mwh, net_import_share_pct (of the BA's
  demand, seven ISO BAs only). BA entity eia930:<BA>: net_import_pairs_mwh,
  net_import_total_interchange_mwh, net_import_balance_mwh (demand less net
  generation) and each _share_pct, days_held, days_left_out, thin_month. The
  headline is the pair sum. CAISO's balance reads about 10 points higher than
  its flows from December 2025: EIA's published net generation for CAISO
  dropped then; say so if asked about CAISO's imports. Last 430 days in the
  live set.
**Battery storage** (session 31, method docs/methods/storage.md):
  eia930_all_storage: EIA-930 hourly net generation of battery storage (fuel
  type BAT), net_generation_battery_mw, MW, positive discharging, negative
  charging; ba = erco, isne, miso, swpp, us48, each from its series start
  (2024-11 for ERCO, ISNE and US48, 2025-01 MISO, 2026-02 SWPP). CISO, NYIS and
  PJM report no BAT series (CAISO: caiso_battery_storage).
  storage_daily_cycle (derived): per complete local day and BA,
  mwh_discharged, mwh_charged, peak_discharge_hour and peak_charge_hour (unit
  hour: local hour of the day, the hour's start), round_trip_ratio (energy
  out over energy in as reported; not a measured efficiency). Since session
  34 also CAISO (ba ciso, entity caiso:ISO, source
  erw:storage_daily_cycle_caiso), from CAISO's own caiso_battery_storage
  (5-minute Total batteries averaged to hours, Pacific days), not EIA-930.
  storage_capacity (derived, entities): every battery unit in EIA-860M,
  operating, under_construction, planned and retired, with capacity_mw
  (nameplate), state, balancing_authority, iso, planned_year, and since
  session 34 energy_capacity_mwh (EIA's Nameplate Energy Capacity, MWh) for
  operating and retired units; EIA-860M gives none for planned units.
**Emissions** (session 32, method docs/methods/emissions.md):
  eia930_all_emissions: EIA's hourly CO2 estimates for EIA-930, from its
  per-BA Grid Monitor workbooks, tCO2 (metric tons): co2_emissions_generated
  (all sources in the BA) and co2_emissions_consumed (generated plus imported
  minus exported); since session 34 also by fuel, co2_emissions_coal,
  co2_emissions_natural_gas, co2_emissions_oil, co2_emissions_other (each only
  where EIA gives it: no oil for ERCOT or MISO), and co2_emissions_imported,
  co2_emissions_exported; ba = ciso, erco, isne, miso, nyis, pjm, swpp, us48;
  from 2018-07-02. These are EIA's estimates (generation by fuel x emission
  factors), not measurements. carbon_intensity_hourly, carbon_intensity_daily
  and carbon_intensity_monthly (session 34; derived, kgCO2/MWh):
  intensity_generation (CO2 generated / EIA's net generation) and
  intensity_demand (CO2 consumed / EIA's demand), from 2018-07; since session
  34 the denominators are the same EIA workbooks' Demand and Net generation
  columns. Monthly: UTC months whose every day is complete.
**EIA petroleum and gas series** (full history, replaced each run):
  eia_fuel_spot_prices: eia:henry_hub (USD/MMBtu), eia:wti_cushing and
    eia:brent (USD/bbl), daily trading dates from 1986 (Henry Hub from 1997)
  eia_product_spot_prices (USD/gal, daily): EER_EPMRU_PF4_Y35NY_DPG NY Harbor
    conventional regular gasoline, EER_EPMRU_PF4_RGC_DPG Gulf Coast gasoline,
    EER_EPMRR_PF4_Y05LA_DPG LA RBOB, EER_EPD2DXL0_PF4_Y35NY_DPG and _RGC_ ULSD,
    EER_EPD2DC_PF4_Y05LA_DPG LA CARB diesel, EER_EPJK_PF4_RGC_DPG Gulf jet
    fuel, EER_EPD2F_PF4_Y35NY_DPG NY heating oil, EER_EPLLPA_PF4_Y44MB_DPG
    Mont Belvieu propane
  eia_retail_fuel_prices (USD/gal, weekly): EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPG regular
    gasoline, EMM_EPM0_PTE_NUS_DPG all grades, EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPG diesel
  eia_petroleum_stocks_weekly (kbbl): WCESTUS1 crude excluding SPR, WCSSTUS1
    SPR, WCRSTUS1 crude total, WGTSTUS1 gasoline, WDISTUS1 distillate,
    WKJSTUS1 jet, WPRSTUS1 propane, WTTSTUS1 crude and products
  eia_petroleum_trade_weekly (kbbl/d): WCRIMUS2 crude imports, WCREXUS2 crude
    exports, WCRNTUS2 crude net imports, WRPIMUS2, WRPEXUS2, WTTIMUS2, WTTEXUS2
  eia_crude_imports_by_country (kbbl/d, monthly): MCRIMUS2 total, and
    MCRIMUS<country>2 by country (MCRIMUSCA2 Canada, MCRIMUSMX2 Mexico, ...)
  eia_crude_first_purchase_prices, eia_padd_crude_pipeline_flows (monthly)
  eia_lng_exports_monthly: export volume (MMcf) and price (USD/Mcf) by terminal
  eia_retail_electricity_prices (USD/MWh, monthly): entity
    eia:retail_price:<state or region>:<sector>, sector RES, COM, IND, TRA,
    OTH or ALL (TX:RES = Texas residential)
  eia_retail_sales_monthly (session 18, monthly): entity
    eia:retail_sales:<state>:<sector> (MWh, from EIA's million kWh x 1000) and
    eia:customers:<state>:<sector> (count), variables retail_sales and
    customers; sectors as above (Form EIA-861M)
  eia_sector_energy_consumption_monthly (session 18, TBtu, US, monthly): MER
    series TEICBUS industrial total energy, TNICBUS industrial end use,
    ESICBUS industrial electricity sales, LOICBUS, NNICBUS, PAICBUS, CLICBUS,
    REICBUS, and commercial TECCBUS, TNCCBUS, ESCCBUS, NNCCBUS, PACCBUS, RECCBUS
  The header's `Series:` line names every series ID in a table.
**Generation by state, monthly** (session 18, MWh, from 2001):
  eia_state_generation_monthly (EIA-923, all sectors): entity
    eia:generation:<location>:<fueltypeid>, fueltypeid ALL, COW, PET, NG, OOG,
    NUC, HYC, HPS, WND, SUN, GEO, BIO, OTH (these twelve add up to ALL) and DPV
    (estimated small-scale solar, NOT in ALL); location = state, DC, PR, US or
    an EIA census region (geo empty)
  state_generation_mix_monthly (derived, method docs/methods/generation_mix.md):
    entity eia:<state> or eia:US, variable net_generation_<group>_mwh for coal,
    natural_gas, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, other_renewables, oil_and_other,
    and not_itemized (EIA's total minus the groups, when EIA withheld a source).
    The groups plus not_itemized equal EIA's total. States only; never ISOs.
**EIA-930 latest hours** (session 18): eia930_generation_latest, a snapshot of
  the last 48 hours' complete hours per BA (same variables as the generation
  tables). The current day so far; complete days are in eia930_all_generation.
**Curtailment** (session 18, MWh, method docs/methods/curtailment.md): the
  three ISOs' figures mean different things; never add them up.
  caiso_curtailment_daily (caiso:ISO, from 2014-05): curtailed_{solar,wind}_mwh,
    by reason curtailed_<fuel>_{local,system}_mwh (2024 on), and
    {solar,wind}_generation_mwh. CAISO's figure.
  spp_curtailment_daily (spp:SPP, spp:SWPW, from 2014): curtailed_<fuel>_
    {redispatch,manual,economic}_mwh and their sum curtailed_<fuel>_mwh. SPP's.
  ercot_wind_solar_hsl_daily (ercot:system, from September 2026 only):
    <fuel>_generation_mwh, <fuel>_hsl_mwh, <fuel>_below_hsl_mwh. ERCOT
    publishes no curtailment: "below HSL" is the ERW's estimate; call it that.
  iso_curtailment_monthly (derived): the same entities and variables summed over
    complete months. MISO publishes no curtailment series.
**FRED**: fred_daily_spot_prices (public; DCOILWTICO, DCOILBRENTEU, DHHNGSP,
  the same EIA spot prices as republished by FRED); fred_imf_commodity_prices
  (INTERNAL; IMF monthly coal, European and Japanese gas, nickel, uranium).
**Capacity, carbon and shipping, all INTERNAL**: pjm_rpm_capacity_prices (PJM
  capacity auction clearing prices by zone and delivery year, USD/MW-day, ts =
  June 1 of the delivery year), carb_auction_allowance_prices (California),
  rggi_auction_allowance_prices (RGGI), portwatch_chokepoint_transits (daily
  ship transits of Hormuz, Suez, Panama).
**Capacity prices, four markets, INTERNAL** (session 65): iso_all_capacity_prices,
  one row per market, zone, delivery period and auction, the clearing price as
  published. market = pjm_bra (entity pjm:<LDA>, USD/MW-day, ts = June 1 of the
  delivery year), nyiso_icap_spot (nyiso:NYCA, nyiso:G-J Locality, nyiso:NYC,
  nyiso:LI, USD/kW-month, monthly from 2018, UCAP basis), isone_fca
  (isone:System-wide or a zone, USD/kW-month, ts = June 1 of the commitment
  period), miso_pra (miso:Z1 to miso:Z10 and miso:ERZ, USD/MW-day, by season,
  planning years 2024/25 on). ALWAYS read the unit column: the table holds two
  units and converts nothing. USD/MW-day x 365 / 12 / 1000 = USD/kW-month.
  x_period_end is the delivery period's last day. ERCOT has no capacity market
  (energy-only) and California has none either: no rows, and that is not a gap.
**Ancillary service prices, day-ahead, hourly, public** (session 65):
  ercot_as_prices (entity ercot:REGUP, ercot:REGDN, ercot:RRS, ercot:NSPIN,
  ercot:ECRS from June 2023; variable mcpc_dam; 2018 on) and caiso_as_prices
  (entity caiso:AS_CAISO, caiso:AS_CAISO_EXP; variables as_price_dam_ru,
  as_price_dam_rd, as_price_dam_sr, as_price_dam_nr; from 2024-09-01). Unit
  USD/MW-hour: dollars per MW of capacity held for one hour, NOT an energy
  price; never add it to USD/MWh. A day short of an hour is left out, not
  filled. Method: docs/methods/capacity_and_ancillary.md.
**The battery revenue stack, derived, public** (session 67):
  battery_stack_monthly, what 1 MW of a grid battery earned per local month
  from energy and ancillary services together, split hour by hour by one
  linear program a day so nothing is counted twice. Entities ercot:HB_HUBAVG
  (2018 on) and caiso:TH_SP15_GEN-APND (2024-09 on). variable is
  <strategy>_<N>h_<metric>: strategy foresight (perfect foresight, an upper
  bound: real-time energy, day-ahead ancillary) or dayahead (the day-ahead
  schedule); N is 2, 4 or 8 hours; metric revenue_energy_usd_per_mw,
  revenue_ancillary_usd_per_mw, revenue_total_usd_per_mw,
  revenue_<product>_usd_per_mw (regup, regdn, rrs, ecrs, nspin in ERCOT;
  regup, regdn, spin, nonspin in CAISO), discharged_mwh_per_mw, days_held,
  days_left_out, days_in_month. Example: foresight_4h_revenue_total_usd_per_mw.
  USD/MW per month: divide by 1000 for USD per kW, sum twelve months for a
  year. A day missing any price is left out and counted, never filled; a
  month's revenue is its held days only. Reserves are paid and never called,
  and the battery is a price taker, so large sizes are overstated: say so.
  ERCOT's February 2021 (Winter Storm Uri) is far above every other month.
  No capacity payment is in it. battery_stack_stress_daily holds the same per
  day for ERCOT's Uri, Elliott and 2023 heat windows (column event).
  Method: docs/methods/battery_stack.md.
**Entities**: eia860m_operating_generators, eia860m_planned_generators
  (status planned or under_construction), eia860m_retired_generators: one row
  per generator, with state, technology_group (natural_gas, solar, wind,
  storage, coal, nuclear, hydro, ...), nameplate_mw, lat/lon, from EIA-860M;
  energy_capacity_mwh (session 34, storage units; empty in the planned table).
  <iso>_interconnection_queue for caiso, ercot, isone, miso, nyiso, spp: one
  row per queue position, capacity_mw, status (active, completed, withdrawn;
  SPP also suspended; ERCOT lists no withdrawn projects), fuel and county as
  the ISO writes them.
**Project map** (session 16, derived, public): energy_projects, one row per
  EIA-860M operating or planned generator and per ISO queue position (kind
  operating, planned, queue), with technology_group, mw, status, state, county,
  lat/lon and geo_precision (point: EIA's coordinates; county: the county's
  Census internal point, for queue positions; none: not placed).
**Datacenters** (session 16, public): datacenter_projects, one row per
  datacenter facility named in the news: operator, developer, site_name, state,
  county, city, mw, project_status (announced, applied, permitted,
  under_construction, operating, cancelled; session 17: "applied" is an
  application filed, not yet granted, and a status is kept only with the words
  that state it), planned_year, power_source, utility, story_urls. Every
  field only as a story states it; blank is "not stated", not zero.
  Session 22: datacenter_facilities (derived, public) is the tracker's one
  table: the news facilities (kind news), the operators' own public site lists
  (kind operator: datacenter_operator_sites, from Amazon Web Services,
  Microsoft Azure, Google, Meta, Oracle, Digital Realty, Equinix, Vantage and
  Switch; QTS, CoreWeave and Crusoe publish no list that can be read) and ISO
  queue positions that name a datacenter or large load (kind queue:
  datacenter_queue_positions), deduplicated by operator plus location. kinds
  lists every source of a row, member_ids and source_urls every member. mw only
  where a story or the operator states it (mw_span holds the operator's exact
  words); queue_mw is a queue position's generation or storage MW, never the
  load. Use it for "how many datacenters", "where", "who"; most rows state no MW,
  so a MW sum covers only the rows that state one.
**Deals** (session 15, public): energy_deals, one row per transaction reported
  in the news: deal_type, buyer, seller, asset, technology, mw, dollars,
  status, story_urls. Same rule: blank is "not stated".
**Events**: news_index (public): one row per scored news story with source,
  sector, region, significance and ai_power_relevance (0 to 10), headline.
  news_stories (INTERNAL) adds titles and summaries of third-party articles.
  The Energy Digest (docs/digest/) is written from them Monday to Friday (no
  weekend issue; session 23), ending with a verified fun fact
  (warehouse/news/facts/), and on Sundays at 23:00 UTC the weekly brief, the
  Energy Roundup (docs/roundup/YYYY-Www.md; the site's /roundup; until session
  23 it was Energy Week on Mondays, docs/weekly/, and /weekly redirects).
**Policy** (session 24, public): policy_actions, one row per energy rule,
  proposed rule or notice in the Federal Register (DOE, FERC, EPA, NRC, BLM,
  Interior; EPA, BLM and Interior only on energy subjects) and per news release
  of NRC, DOE, the Texas PUC and the CPUC, since 2025-10-01: agency,
  action_type, title, docket (docket ids and RINs), sector_tags, states, links
  to the news stories that report it, and significance (0 to 10, the news
  rubric). policy_reads: impact reads of actions scored 5 or more (what
  changes, affected sectors, ISOs and states, direction of effect on supply,
  demand, prices and buildout, timeline, a plain read); a blank field was
  dropped because its quoted words were not in the action's own text.
**Companies** (session 25, public): energy_companies, one row per company the
  Thesis Builder (tool 27) found in a niche it mapped: name, one-line
  description, niche_tags, stage, raised, location, founders, website, sources
  (links) and a confidence score (0 to 100) with the clause that explains it.
  A seed, not a census. Since session 27 it also holds every party of
  energy_deals (buyers, sellers, other parties): those rows carry the deals'
  sector, tags, place (where the deal is) and story links, and a
  confidence_note starting "from deals; not yet researched", with no
  description, founders, stage or raised. Session 28: a party that is not a
  company name (a description such as "bond investors", a country, a
  government body, a law) is left out, and stays in energy_deals; a party
  naming several companies is split into them. A number that no cited source
  confirmed reads "not confirmed". A public company's raised is
  blank and its confidence_note starts "public company" (session 26). The
  site's /companies shows it.
**Weather** (session 24, public): weather_obs_hourly (observed, the NWS API
  keeps about 7 days, the table grows daily) and weather_forecast_hourly (the
  latest 7-day hourly forecast): temperature_f (degF) and wind_speed_mph at one
  airport per ISO load center (entity nws:<station>, node the ISO: ERCOT KDFW,
  CAISO KLAX, NYISO KLGA, ISO-NE KBOS, PJM KPHL, MISO KIND, SPP KOKC).
**Batteries** (session 23, public): caiso_battery_storage, CAISO's own Today's
  Outlook battery output, 5-minute, MW (positive discharge, negative charging),
  from 2025-08. EIA-930 has no battery series for any ISO in the warehouse.
**Automated Analysis** (session 23, tool 26): ten chart templates
  (warehouse/analysis/templates/) run every Sunday; a rule (robust z of each
  headline against its own history) picks the chart of the week. Results are
  in docs/analysis/YYYY-Www/ (results.json holds every template's headline and
  chart) and on the site's /analysis. They are computed from the tables above;
  cite the tables they name, not the analysis files.


## 3. Which table for which question

| Question | Table |
|---|---|
| Winter Storm Uri (ERCOT, February 2021) day by day against the same days of 2019 and 2020: prices, demand served, net generation, carbon intensity | `event_window_daily` (event uri_2021) |
| What does a 100 MW datacenter pay for energy in ERCOT (or another ISO): wholesale energy, load-weighted and flat, by month and hour of day | `cost_of_power_monthly`, `cost_of_power_hourly_profile` (and `cost_of_power_carbon` for cost against carbon) |
| COVID-19, spring 2020: demand served in the seven ISO grids and US48 against the same weekday of 2019, by day and by week, in MWh and percent | `event_window_daily` (event covid_2020) |
| The August 2020 heat wave in CAISO, Winter Storm Elliott (December 2022, six grids) or the summer 2023 heat in ERCOT: demand, peak hour and intensity against the same weekdays of earlier years, ERCOT hub prices | `event_window_daily` (events caiso_heat_2020, elliott_2022, ercot_heat_2023) |
| A recent ISO price (last month) | `iso_{dam,rtm}_hub_prices` (market), `{nyiso,isone}_{dam,rtm}_zone_prices` |
| ERCOT price before the live window, or a year | `ercot_all_hub_prices_history` (market, year) |
| ERCOT distribution: percentiles, IQR, scarcity or negative counts by year or month | `ercot_peak_premium_annual` / `_monthly` |
| Demand, generation mix | `eia930_all_demand` / `eia930_all_generation` (ba) |
| Henry Hub, WTI, Brent | `eia_fuel_spot_prices` (FRED copy: `fred_daily_spot_prices`) |
| Gasoline, diesel, jet, propane wholesale | `eia_product_spot_prices`; retail pump prices `eia_retail_fuel_prices` |
| Crude and product stocks, trade | `eia_petroleum_stocks_weekly`, `eia_petroleum_trade_weekly`, `eia_crude_imports_by_country` |
| LNG exports | `eia_lng_exports_monthly` |
| Retail electricity price by state | `eia_retail_electricity_prices` |
| Electricity sales or customers by state and sector | `eia_retail_sales_monthly` |
| Industrial or commercial energy use, all fuels (US) | `eia_sector_energy_consumption_monthly` |
| Generation mix of a state, monthly since 2001 | `state_generation_mix_monthly` (EIA codes: `eia_state_generation_monthly`) |
| Generation mix of an ISO today, or this week | `eia930_generation_latest`, `eia930_all_generation` (ba) |
| Power flowing between balancing authorities (imports, exports, interchange, ties) | `eia930_all_interchange` (ba), `grid_network_links`, `grid_network_nodes` |
| Who supplies a grid, by neighbour and month; net imports as a share of demand | `ba_supply_monthly`, `eia930_daily_total_interchange`, `eia930_daily_interchange` |
| How much of an event's effect on demand or price is the weather (temperature-controlled event study estimates) | `event_study_estimates` (x_spec dow_year_temp_v1 beside dow_year_mean_v1) |
| Temperature at an airport on the days of an event or its baseline | `event_window_daily` (entity noaa:<station>), `noaa_isd_hourly` |
| CAISO's Flex Alerts, Restricted Maintenance Operations, EEAs and stage emergencies, 1998 on (days, types, regions) | `caiso_grid_emergencies` (events; event_type flex_alert, rmo, eea1 to eea3, stage1 to stage3...) |
| How tight CAISO's evenings were: peak demand, the evening ramp, batteries' share of the evening peak, the day's notices | `caiso_reliability_daily` (eia930:CISO and caiso:ISO, daily since 2018-07-01) |
| CAISO's September 2022 heat wave | `event_window_daily` and `event_study_estimates` (event caiso_heat_2022) |
| The January 2025 cold (six grids) or the June 2025 heat (four eastern grids), with the MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE and SPP hubs' prices | `event_window_daily` and `event_study_estimates` (events cold_2025, east_heat_2025) |
| EIA-930 demand or net generation in January to June 2018 | `eia930_all_history` |
| Battery charging and discharging by hour or day; the battery fleet by state, ISO or year | `eia930_all_storage`, `storage_daily_cycle`, `storage_capacity` |
| What a grid battery earns from energy and ancillary services, by month, duration and strategy | `battery_stack_monthly`, `battery_stack_stress_daily` |
| CO2 emissions of an ISO's power, and its carbon intensity (kg CO2 per MWh) | `eia930_all_emissions` (since 2018-07), `carbon_intensity_hourly` / `_daily` (last ~30 days) |
| Day-ahead against real-time, on-peak prices, heat rates, volatility by hub | `iso_trader_daily` (market), `iso_rt_top_intervals` |
| A hub's latest daily mean, its move, 7- and 30-day averages, peak and off-peak, spark spread, Brent minus WTI | `price_board_latest`, `price_board_peak_offpeak`, `price_board_spreads` |
| Wind and solar curtailment | `caiso_curtailment_daily`, `spp_curtailment_daily`, `ercot_wind_solar_hsl_daily` (not curtailment: output below HSL), `iso_curtailment_monthly` |
| Battery output (CAISO) | `caiso_battery_storage` |
| Federal rules, notices, agency and PUC news releases; their impact | `policy_actions`, `policy_reads` |
| Temperature or wind at an ISO load center, observed or forecast | `weather_obs_hourly`, `weather_forecast_hourly` |
| Energy companies (startups, their stage and funding) found by the Thesis Builder | `energy_companies` |
| Power plants, capacity by state or fuel | `eia860m_*_generators` |
| Projects waiting to connect | `<iso>_interconnection_queue` |
| All generators and queue positions with a location | `energy_projects` |
| Datacenter facilities (operator, place, MW), all sources | `datacenter_facilities` (news only: `datacenter_projects`; operator lists: `datacenter_operator_sites`) |
| Energy deals (PPAs, M&A, financings) | `energy_deals` |
| News, deals, policy stories | `news_index` |
| Capacity, carbon, shipping | internal tables above; say they are internal |

Not in the warehouse today: PJM energy prices (day-ahead and real-time), SPP
real-time before 2026-09-24 (iso_rtm_hub_prices, market spp_rtm, starts
then), CAISO or NYISO before the live window, futures, lithium and
other battery metals, equities, EIA-930 CO2 by fuel and imported or exported
CO2 as separate series (in EIA's workbooks, not yet in the warehouse), carbon
intensity before the last 30 days, battery energy capacity in MWh, and a list
of ERCOT large-load interconnection
requests by site (ERCOT publishes only aggregates: Protocol 3.2.7).
Say "not in the warehouse" rather than approximating from another table.


## 4. The things that silently produce wrong answers

1. **ts_utc is the interval START.** ISOs label "hour ending"; the ERW has
   converted. Do not shift again; the end is ts_utc + freq. EIA-930 labels hours
   by their end; the ERW subtracted one hour.
2. **Operating days are local.** Convert before grouping by day, month or year:
   ERCOT and SPP America/Chicago, CAISO America/Los_Angeles, NYISO and ISO-NE
   America/New_York, MISO fixed EST (Etc/GMT+5). An ERCOT day runs 05:00Z to
   05:00Z (CDT) or 06:00Z to 06:00Z (CST). EIA-930 tables hold whole UTC days.
3. **Real-time values differ in kind.** `lmp_rtm_15m_mean` (CAISO, NYISO,
   ISO-NE) is the ERW's time-weighted mean of the ISO's 5-minute prices, not a
   published price, and smoother than it. `spp_rtm` (ERCOT) is ERCOT's own
   15-minute settlement point price, reserve adders included; a hub price is an
   average over its buses. `lmp_rtm` (MISO, ISO-NE hourly) is an hourly price.
   Compare like with like and name the variable.
4. **Day-ahead tables run past today** (the next day's auction). When joining
   day-ahead to real-time, inner-join on ts_utc.
5. **A missing table or row is not zero.** Tables are written only when every
   node has every interval (per day where a connector backfills day by day).
   `warehouse/metadata/run_status.csv` records every run and every gap.
6. **Spans differ by table and move daily.** Use `ts_min`/`ts_max` from
   coverage, or the data, never the "Window" header line alone.
7. **Names are exact strings.** "N.Y.C.", "HUD VL" (with a space),
   ".Z.MAINE", "TH_NP15_GEN-APND". EIA entities are EIA series IDs.
8. **Negative prices and spikes above 1,000 USD/MWh are real.** Report median
   and quantiles beside a mean; do not drop outliers without saying so.
9. **Units vary**: USD/MWh, MW, USD/MMBtu, USD/bbl, USD/gal, kbbl, kbbl/d,
   MMcf, USD/Mcf, USD/MW-day, USD/tCO2 (CARB), USD/short_ton (RGGI), count,
   dwt. Read `unit`; never convert silently.
10. **Snapshots**: entities tables describe one vintage (the EIA-860M month,
   the queue download date). Counts are "as of" that vintage.


## 5. License

Every table is `public` or `internal` (`erw.coverage()["license"]`). Internal
means licensed for internal use only: PJM data, CARB, RGGI, IMF series via
FRED, PortWatch, the third-party text in news_stories, and the ERW's own
operating tables (api_cost_ledger, news_scores_shadow), which are never data
for an answer. Never publish or
redistribute an internal table; label any number from one as internal. A
derived table takes the most restrictive license of its inputs. For anything
public, `erw.filter(license="public")`.

Provenance tier (session 28): every table is `source` (as the publisher
published it), `derived` (computed by the ERW from other tables, method in
docs/methods/) or `model_extracted` (at least one field written by a model
reading news, filings or the web: energy_deals, datacenter_projects,
datacenter_facilities, policy_reads, energy_companies, and the scores in
news_stories, news_index and policy_actions). `erw.tier(name)`, the `tier`
column of `erw.coverage()`, and every tool result give it. A number from a
model_extracted table is the model's reading of the linked source, not the
source's figure: say "model-extracted" next to it.


## 6. Reading the data

    pip install "git+https://github.com/SamuelEnrique/erw.git#subdirectory=package"
    # or, from a clone: python -m pip install -e package

    import erw
    erw.info()                            # summary: tables, rows, data version
    erw.coverage()                        # one row per table: iso, market, n_nodes,
                                          # interval, ts_min, ts_max, n_rows,
                                          # source_report, last_run, validator_status,
                                          # license, sector, derived, tier
    erw.fetch("ercot_all_hub_prices_history", market="ercot_rtm", year=2025, node="HB_WEST")
    erw.fetch("eia930_all_demand", ba="ciso")   # partition filters: market, ba, year
    erw.fetch("eia_fuel_spot_prices", start="2026-09-01", end="2026-09-08")
    erw.filter(iso="ERCOT", market="rtm") # table names; also variable, node,
    erw.filter(sector="oil", license="public")   # start, end, license, sector
    erw.sources("iso_dam_hub_prices")     # reports, report pages, file URLs
    erw.cite("iso_dam_hub_prices")        # citation: publisher, report, table, version, tier
    erw.tier("energy_deals")              # source, derived or model_extracted
    erw.version()                         # which data you read

Backends (`ERW_BACKEND`, or `erw.set_backend(...)`); the calls do not change:
- `local` (default): the CSVs in the repository's warehouse/output, or ERW_DATA_DIR.
- `redivis`: the Redivis dataset `energy_research_warehouse`, the store of
  record, every table, full history (REDIVIS_API_TOKEN, REDIVIS_OWNER).
- `supabase`: the live set behind the public site: public tables, the last 35
  days of ISO prices and EIA-930 (session 36C; 90 before) (and all eight CO2 variables of
  eia930_all_emissions, session 36A), and the derived, fuel, queue and news
  tables whole (SUPABASE_URL with the anon or service key). Not in it: the ERCOT
  history (ercot_all_hub_prices_history) and eia860m_operating_generators
  and eia860m_planned_generators; read those from local files or Redivis, or
  use energy_projects (every operating and planned generator) from Supabase.
Sectors for `filter`: power, gas, oil, products, lng, coal, uranium, carbon,
capacity, metals, equities, news, deals, datacenters.


## 7. The public site and the chat

The site (site/, Next.js) shows the latest real-time price per hub (the
Supabase table latest_prices, refreshed every 15 minutes: variable spp_rtm for
ERCOT, lmp_rtm_5min for the others; CAISO's newest 5-minute price can start
just after it is fetched, as CAISO publishes it ahead of its interval), the price
tables, the digest archive, coverage, methods and the ERCOT peak-premium
explorer. `/ask` answers questions with the tools of warehouse/chat
(list_tables, describe_table, query, compare, and grid_notes): every number in
an answer must come from a tool result, and every answer cites its tables.
Today's prices (session 58): the price tables the chat reads hold complete
operating days, through yesterday at best (the daily run loads them). Today's
real-time prices exist only in latest_prices, the 15-minute snapshot on /board
and /prices, which the chat does not read. For today's price, say it is not in
the tables the chat reads, give the newest day they hold, and point to /board.

**Event windows** (session 36B, derived, public, method docs/methods/events.md):
  event_window_daily, daily figures around an event and the same calendar days
  of earlier years, partition columns ba and event. The first event is uri_2021
  (Winter Storm Uri, ERCOT): operating days 2021-02-07 to 2021-02-24 and the
  same days of 2019 and 2020. Variables: rt_mean, rt_max, da_mean, da_max
  (ercot:HB_HUBAVG, USD/MWh); demand_mwh, demand_min_mw, demand_max_mw,
  net_generation_mwh, intensity_generation (eia930:ERCO); for event days
  demand_mwh_vs_baseline, net_generation_mwh_vs_baseline (the day minus the mean
  of 2019 and 2020) and *_day_change (the day minus the day before). Demand
  during load shed is load served, not what customers wanted. The site's
  /events and /events/uri-2021 draw it.
  The key is (entity, variable, ts_utc, event) since session 36C: filter by
  event. The second event (session 36C) is covid_2020: eia930:CISO, ERCO, ISNE,
  MISO, NYIS, PJM, SWPP and US48, each BA's local day 2020-03-01 to 2020-05-31,
  against the same weekday 364 days earlier (2019; the 728-day baseline of 2018
  is not held, EIA's workbooks start 2018-07-01). Variables: demand_mwh,
  demand_min_mw, demand_max_mw, intensity_generation (window and baseline days);
  demand_mwh_vs_baseline and demand_pct_vs_baseline (unit pct) for event days;
  demand_mwh_vs_baseline_week and demand_pct_vs_baseline_week (freq P1W, at the
  week's Sunday, 13 whole weeks); rt_mean and da_mean of ercot:HB_HUBAVG. One
  baseline year: 2019's weather is in every comparison, and the warehouse holds
  no weather for it. /events/covid-2020 draws it.
  Session 39 adds three events with the same weekday-aligned baseline (364 and
  728 days earlier, both held), without weekly rows, and with the peak hour
  against the baseline (demand_max_mw_vs_baseline, MW; demand_max_pct_vs_baseline,
  pct): caiso_heat_2020 (eia930:CISO, 2020-08-10 to 2020-08-24, no prices: CAISO's
  2020 prices are not held), elliott_2022 (eia930:PJM, MISO, SWPP, NYIS, ISNE,
  ERCO, 2022-12-19 to 2022-12-29, with ercot:HB_HUBAVG rt_mean, rt_max, da_mean,
  da_max) and ercot_heat_2023 (eia930:ERCO, 2023-08-01 to 2023-09-10, the same
  hub prices). Pages /events/caiso-heat-2020, /events/elliott-2022 and
  /events/ercot-heat-2023 say where the rows contradict the headline story.
  Session 49: covid_2020's 728-day baseline (2018-03-04 to 2018-06-03) is
  restored for the seven ISO BAs from eia930_all_history (EIA's six-month file,
  2018 January to June, demand_mw and net_generation_mw, the Adjusted columns);
  US48 keeps 2019 alone. Weather rows for every event, window and baseline
  days: entity noaa:<station> (DFW, IAH, SAC, LAX, PHL, ORD, MSP, JFK, BOS,
  OKC), ba the grid it stands for, variables temp_mean_f, temp_min_f,
  temp_max_f (degF) and hdd_65f, cdd_65f (degF-day, from (max + min) / 2), from
  noaa_isd_hourly (NOAA NCEI ISD, temperature_f and dew_point_f per
  observation, public domain).

**Event studies** (session 47, derived, public, method docs/methods/event_study.md):
  event_study_estimates, partition columns ba and event: for each event and
  grid, <outcome>_effect_day (each event day) and <outcome>_effect_pooled (the
  window), outcome demand_mwh (MWh a day) or rt_mean (ERCOT hub, USD/MWh), with
  x_std_error, x_ci_low, x_ci_high (95 percent), x_n and x_spec;
  <outcome>_counterfactual_mean; demand_mw_effect_hNN by local hour. x_spec
  dow_year_mean_v1: event-day indicators, weekday and year effects. Session 49
  adds dow_year_temp_v1 (the grid's heating and cooling degree days and their
  squares; variables *_effect_day_temp, *_effect_pooled_temp,
  *_counterfactual_mean_temp; none for US48, which has no station) and
  dow_trend_v1 (*_effect_pooled_trend: a linear trend in place of the year
  effects, a robustness row). The /events pages show both estimates.

**Cost of power** (session 37, derived, public, method docs/methods/cost_of_power.md):
  market-based, wholesale energy only (no transmission, distribution, capacity
  or taxes; no LCOE). Per ISO main hub (ercot:HB_HUBAVG, caiso:TH_SP15_GEN-APND,
  isone:.H.INTERNAL_HUB, miso:INDIANA.HUB, nyiso:N.Y.C., spp:SPPNORTH_HUB; no
  PJM, internal) and local month: cost_of_power_monthly holds rt_ and
  da_load_weighted (hourly price x the BA's EIA-930 demand, over demand),
  rt_ and da_simple_mean (what a flat load pays), rt_ and da_shape_premium, rt_
  and da_hours and hours_in_month (a month is complete when rt_hours equals
  hours_in_month). ERCOT from 2018-07; the other five ISOs hold about the last
  33 days, so their months are partial. cost_of_power_hourly_profile:
  rt_mean_h00 to rt_mean_h23 (mean real-time price by local hour of day, last
  12 months held) and rt_days_hNN. cost_of_power_carbon: rt_load_weighted
  beside intensity_demand and intensity_generation. A 100 MW load at load
  factor 0.9 for 90 days draws 194,400 MWh; its flat-load cost is that times
  the hours-weighted mean of rt_simple_mean over the last 12 months held.
  /cost-of-power draws it.

**Grid pages** (session 35): /grid/ercot, /grid/caiso, /grid/pjm, /grid/nyiso,
/grid/isone, /grid/miso, /grid/spp, one template for students: demand now,
generation by fuel, batteries, carbon intensity, hub prices (PJM's are
internal, not shown), the interconnection queue and datacenters, and the news,
each block only where the warehouse holds that grid's rows. Their config is
docs/grids/grids.json (which tables carry each grid). Each has a written layer,
docs/grids/<grid>.md: who runs it, how prices are set, what is different, three
dated events, a glossary, each section citing ISO and EIA pages; it is text,
not data (tier written), and the grid_notes tool reads it. /ask?grid=<grid> is
the page's scoped chat: its tools see only that grid's tables and rows
(partition ba, market prefix, storage_capacity's iso, energy_projects' queue).
A datacenter facility counts for a grid (session 36A) when it comes from that
grid's queue, else when its utility is one the grid lists in grids.json, else
by the grid's states (docs/methods/datacenter_facilities.md, "Grid pages").
Each dated event of the written layer cites the ISO, EIA or FERC page that
states it; three are given as a year only because no such page states the day.


## 8. Working well

- Find the table first (coverage or list_tables with a sector or ISO filter),
  then check its span. If the live table does not cover the period, look for a
  yearly or derived table before saying the data is missing.
- Print summaries, not whole tables (NYISO real-time is over 30,000 rows).
- State the table, entity, variable, period (UTC and local) and unit behind
  every number, and whether a value is derived (a mean, a percentile).
- A surprising number: read `df.attrs["erw"]["notes"]` and the run log before
  calling it an error.


## 9. Citing

The numbers belong to the organizations that published them. Cite the source
report, then the ERW table and data version as the route:

    print(erw.cite("ercot_all_hub_prices_history"))

names the publisher, report id and title, report page, retrieval date, table
and data commit. For Redivis, cite the released dataset version. For a
reproducible result also give `erw.version()`: tables change daily.
